query: Can we reliably estimate the boundary entropy exponent β from finite samples? Which practical estimators (empirical covering numbers, box-counting dimension, log-cover growth) perform well?

response.query: Can we reliably estimate the boundary entropy exponent β from finite samples? Which practical estimators (empirical covering numbers, box-counting dimension, log-cover growth) perform well?
response.answer: Estimating the boundary entropy exponent β from finite samples is challenging, but empirical covering numbers and box-counting dimension often perform well as practical estimators. Log-cover growth is also a reliable method.
